request.spec: Exports taken while a preview date is set use the preview figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Exports taken while a preview date is set use the preview figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I didn't need to change any behaviour, because the exports already use the preview figures. The main `preview exports` test passes, but 2 of the 4 tests in the spec still fail, and neither failure involves an export or the preview.

**Why no change was needed:** setting a preview already changes the date that every date-dependent figure on the screen is worked out from.
- The people export (`features/people/export.slot.tsx`) and the claims export (`features/claims/export.slot.tsx`) work out their figures, including late charges, from that date. So they already give the preview numbers: Ada's due goes from 10.00 to 11.00 under a 2026-05-01 preview, and back after clearing.
- The pools export re-reads from the server through `getJson`, which already sends `?preview=`.
- The statement export writes figures that were saved when the statement was made, so a preview doesn't affect it.

The only edit is to the doc comments of the people and claims export components, saying that a preview date carries through to the file.

**Test results** (`bin/e2e`): 2 passed, 2 failed.
- **`preview exports scenario 1` fails because of the test itself.** At line 155 it expects `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. Line 46 sets the parent to `${sheet}-p`, so the screen shows the real sheet id (e.g. `smvlj4w07gavg-p`). That placeholder was never filled in, and the app can't make this pass without the spec being edited.
- **`preview exports scenario 2` fails on an older rule.** At line 542 it expects a claim for Ada dated 2026-03-05 to be refused, but the app accepts it. The only rule I found that might apply is the closed-period one: the claim may run across a period that was closed automatically. The app deliberately doesn't refuse claims for automatically-closed periods (`RefuseClosedNewClaim`, `PeriodRepository.closedByHandFor`). I couldn't confirm that's the rule the test relies on, and I didn't want to loosen a rule an earlier feature set without being sure. The test fails the same way with or without my edit.

**Port problem:** your environment sets `PORT=3002`, and another process is already listening on that port. On the first run the app failed to start, and the tests ran against whatever that other server is. I left that process alone and ran with `PORT=3917 bin/e2e`.
